_what_this_is: The machine-readable register of every measured ArifiLabs win that an upstream bump or a
fork ingest must not silently overwrite. President mandate 2026-09-04, assignment 2.
Read by: arifi_sync.py `protected-win validate|check|discover`, and by `bump` at leg 1b,
which REFUSES when an incoming change collides with an entry and no measured comparison
AUTHORED, NOT GENERATED. protected_paths, anchors, quality_gate and workload are not
derivable from a commit trailer, and a fabricated value would make the guard lie. The
candidate set IS derivable and `protected-win discover` prints it, so a measured win
cannot quietly stay unregistered. An entry that cannot be completed honestly stays out
of this file and stays on that list.

_schema.evidence: a repo- or studio-relative path, or `commit:<sha>` when the measurement table lives in the commit message
_schema.anchors: distinctive symbols/env gates whose REMOVAL by an incoming diff is itself a collision, even when the file survives. Searched in SOURCE only: an anchor names a mechanism in LIVE CODE, so every home that merely RECORDS the name is excluded - `patches/series/` because this fork bakes every mechanism into a generated patch (R6 finding 2); `tools/arifi-sync/` because THIS FILE is tracked and lists every anchor literal by construction, which made the rule structurally unable to report any anchor absent (R6B, the blocking finding); and `*.md` plus root `docs/` because prose is not a mechanism (R6B note N2). Write an anchor that only prose says, and validation will correctly call it absent. Full contract: UPDATE-RUNBOOK 4.3 and the `_anchor_present` docstring
_schema.symbols: OPTIONAL, {"<file>": ["function_or_kernel", ...]}. Each named symbol must have a DEFINITION in that file at the validated ref - a definition-shaped match (name, its parameter list, then `{` after optional qualifiers, or an explicit template instantiation line). A `.cuh`/`.h` declaration ending in `;` or a call site NEVER satisfies it. This is the class the anchor half cannot see (WI-1700): during the R13 b10819 sync `ggml_cuda_moe_cache_mmv_fused` lost its body in ggml-cuda/mmvq.cu while its declaration and caller survived, 41/41 anchors validated, and the fork stopped linking on CUDA (WI-1699). The build catches this on the backends this estate compiles; on CUDA/Metal/SYCL nothing else does. On a miss, validate names the symbol, the file, every surviving mention, and the last commit that touched the definition (`git log -S`). The file need not be in protected_paths - name the file that holds the body, wherever it is
_schema.protected_paths: a file, or a DIRECTORY. A directory is matched on the `<dir>/` boundary against the incoming change, so a whole subtree is genuinely guarded (R6 finding 1). The price is real - ANY touch under a protected subtree refuses until a comparison is recorded - so a subtree is registered only where the tree is ours
_schema.supersession_law: A superseded win is NEVER deleted. It keeps its entry, its evidence and the valid_conditions it still wins under, per the mandate's condition of validity.

wins.mechanism: Tiled CONCAT dispatch for a transposed src1, taken on the delta-net conv state. A dedicated concat_transpose shader plus a selector branch ahead of the pre-existing cpy_transpose_02_32/02_16 tiled branch; the two predicates select disjoint pipelines.
wins.quality_gate: ON-vs-OFF generated text byte-identical at temp 0 / top_k 1 / presence_penalty 0 on the canonical binary (QUALITY-CANON.json, 3/3), F-141 0/8 on every slot (f141-canon/F141.json), test-backend-ops -o CONCAT 195/195 0 FAIL both arms.
wins.workload: Huihui-Qwen3.8-27B-abliterated-UD Q4_K_XL on the seat serve line (-dev Vulkan0 -ngl 999 -fa on -c 8192 -b 1024 -ub 512 -t 16 -tb 32 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 --jinja); op-level receipt via llama-bench -p 2048 -n 0 -ub 512 -ngl 999 -fa 1 -t 16 -r 1 with GGML_VK_PERF_LOGGER=1, Balanced power plan.
wins.measured_effect: CONCAT dispatch -12.79% (-15.66 ms per ub512 prefill graph) on the LANE binary; end-to-end ceiling +0.18%, serve-level TIED on all three shapes across two counterbalanced takes. A canonical-binary re-measurement is banked separately in rank3-r10/71-PERF-CANON.json.
wins.valid_conditions: Fires only where src1 is transposed with nb[0] > nb[1] and src0 ne[2]==ne[3]==1 - the delta-net conv-state shape. test-backend-ops carries no case of that shape, so the suite proves non-regression, not coverage.
wins.notes: The win is op-level and statistically zero at the seat. It is retained anyway: a win is a win even if it is small (mandate root cause 1).

wins.mechanism: Subgroup-cooperative TQ mat-vec. Register WHT via subgroupShuffleXor replaces the 32-thread shared-memory butterfly, removing hot-loop barriers and unpinning the workgroup. The legacy 32-thread shaders remain as the fallback for devices without 32-multiple subgroups.
wins.quality_gate: Build-time CPU/GLSL mirror-pair registration in ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/arifi_sync_check.py (49 -> 52 pairs); float rotated activation throughout, so the mmvq-tq fp16-store bias cannot recur; test-backend-ops TQ coverage green.
wins.workload: 780M, llama-bench/llama-server: 27B tq3_4s tg32, and 0.5b tq4_1s / tq3_1s tg64 (lane-163).
wins.valid_conditions: Devices whose subgroup size is a multiple of 32. Elsewhere the legacy shaders are the correct path and must survive with it.

wins.mechanism: Column-blocked escha_mm: one weight decode serves C columns, removing redundant decode work rather than load pressure. C=8 shipped, with a fall-back to the one-column pipeline below a full block, and every dispatch bounded to 32 columns (the F-124 host-freeze guard).
wins.quality_gate: tests/test-backend-ops.cpp ESCHA_MM cases at real 27B shapes (ncols=9), 10/10 GREEN; the f32->f16 convert must stay float16_t, not packed - a one-ulp truncation there corrupted 25.6% of codewords once already (974d46603).
wins.workload: test-backend-ops perf -b Vulkan0 -o ESCHA_MM, Balanced, one session: escha2 5120x12288 and escha3 17408x5120 at ncols 1 / 8 / 64.
wins.measured_effect: 3.51x on escha3 17408x5120 at ncols=64 (135386 -> 38587 us), 3.09x at ncols=8; decode held at baseline (2856 vs 2831 us at ncols=1) by the threshold.
wins.valid_conditions: Prefill shapes with ncols >= ESCHA_MM_COLS. Below the threshold the one-column pipeline is the winner - C=4 made decode 11-27% SLOWER - so the threshold is part of the win, not an optimisation of it. ESCHA_SG_HADAMARD stays OFF by default: the lever was refuted by measurement.
wins.notes: C=16 is the next untested step and is deliberately not assumed.

wins.mechanism: Full 64-bit pair sourcing plus the row-parity correction in the Escha weight decode. K=2 had windowed a bare u16 where the reference PTX builds a 64-bit pair and windows a 32-bit suffix, so 7 of every 8 weights decoded from truncated data; the tile scatter row term used (c & 1) where the PTX predicate inverts it, which nulled K=3.
wins.quality_gate: Whole-tensor correlation against a known-good GGUF of the same base checkpoint over 25 projections: worst 0.9358, median 0.987, with the positive control run FIRST. End-to-end Vulkan coherence PASSES. A test that compares our two implementations against each other does NOT satisfy this gate - that is precisely what missed both defects.
wins.workload: Escha-W2 native decode, Vulkan path, K=2 and K=3.
wins.measured_effect: Escha-W2 native decode goes from token salad to coherent; worst-projection weight correlation 0.000 -> 0.9358, K=2 and K=3 both correct.
wins.valid_conditions: Escha weight decode at K=2 and K=3. This is a CORRECTNESS win, so an incoming change that is faster but re-truncates the pair sourcing loses outright - speed cannot buy this one back.
wins.notes: Registered because the mandate's protection is of the winning FORMULA, and a decode that is fast and wrong is not a candidate at all.

wins.mechanism: Dual residency for the VNNI weight repack (GGML_ARIFI_VNNI_REPACK=2): keeps the decode win of mode 1 while leaving prefill on its original path, and fixes the hot-path cost that ate the first implementation.
wins.quality_gate: Bit-identical to mode 1 and placement-identical to mode 0 across the correctness sweep. That sweep alone is NOT sufficient - the first version passed it and was slower than doing nothing - so the timed A/B is part of the gate.
wins.workload: RIG-A, llama-server, two g64 models, -ngl 0 --no-host -c 2048 -t 8, 519-token prefill, n_predict 128, temp 0, three interleaved replicates x 5 rolls, roll 1 dropped, n=12 per cell, one binary with only the env flip.
wins.measured_effect: decode +22.0% (mixed) and +23.7% (all-Q2_0) against mode 0, ranges DISJOINT, with prefill held at baseline (958.96 vs 898.11 and 963.51 vs 905.25 prompt t/s, ranges overlapping so no prefill gain is claimed).
wins.valid_conditions: CPU tier, g64 ternary models, -ngl 0. Mode 1 remains the wrong trade on this workload: it pays -65% to -80% of prefill for the same decode.

wins.workload: llama-server, streamed-MoE expert bundle, lane-110C rounds on RIG-A.
wins.measured_effect: server decode climbs 5.99 / 9.79 / 10.48 / 12.31 t/s against the fork's best 9.00 (RESULTS lane-110C).
wins.valid_conditions: Disk-streamed sparse MoE with an expert bundle present. Inert without one.

wins._registered: 2026-09-05, lane-209 rank-3 R6. Was `REGISTRATION OWED` (bca0f5b9a), noted as real and measured; the entry below is that row written out.
wins.mechanism: GPU-safe staging edge for the streamed-MoE pipeline: ggml_moe_pipeline_build_tasks builds its output with ggml_dup, not ggml_view_tensor. A view keeps sharing the source buffer, so with -ngl the CPU-side pipeline op would dereference a device pointer; the dup gives the op its own tensor and lets the scheduler insert the device-to-host copy. Carries the CPU zero-copy path and the LANE110_PROF per-op timing gate alongside it.
wins.quality_gate: The GPU arm must RUN clean, not merely start - the failure this fixes is a segfault on a device pointer, so 'it launched' is not the gate. Coherent output with -ngl 99 -cmoe on the streamed path, lane-110B/C, with the CPU zero-copy arm still coherent in the same round.
wins.workload: RIG-A, llama-server, streamed-MoE expert bundle, -ngl 99 -cmoe; lane-110B/C rounds.
wins.measured_effect: GPU -ngl 99 -cmoe clean at 4.9 t/s with CPU zero-copy retained (RESULTS lane-110B/C).
wins.valid_conditions: Streamed-MoE with any GPU offload in play. With -ngl 0 the dup is redundant but harmless; it must survive anyway, because the defect only appears on the offloaded arm.

wins.mechanism: ROCmFP4 / ROCmFPX serialized weight formats: the format sources and their CPU quant, dequant, validate and vec_dot paths, plus the type ids, ftype ids, quantizer wiring and gguf-py registry that make a ROCmFPX artifact loadable. Adopted verbatim from charlie12345/ROCmFPX so its GGUFs and its convert/quantize tooling interoperate byte-for-byte.
wins.quality_gate: Both ROCmFPX conformance suites pass on our compiler against the ported sources - test_rocmfpx (fp3/fp6/fp8 mse and imatrix weighting) and test_rocmfp2_reference (32520 checks, fingerprint 78389c1c8a0a57a2). Plus the fail-closed half: with the formats compiled OUT, the same artifact must still be REFUSED loudly (`type 100 ((null)) ... not a multiple of block size (0)`), never silently mis-decoded. Round-trip quantizer output for these types is UNMEASURED and is not covered by this gate.
wins.workload: RIG-A, llama-server per F-085, -ngl 0, native artifact models/rocmfpx-trial/ornith-9b-mtp-kl-Q4_0_ROCMFP4_COHERENT.gguf (257 tensors at type-id 100).
wins.measured_effect: CAPABILITY, measured as loadable and correct, not as fast: the native ROCmFP4 artifact loads in llama-server and completes "The capital of France is" with " Paris." at 3.24 tok/s on -ngl 0. No ON-path performance claim is made - throughput is UNMEASURED.
wins.valid_conditions: Builds with GGML_ARIFI_ROCMFPX_FORMATS ON, and any build at all for the ids: the enum values are unconditional ABI on purpose, because a file may carry them regardless of what this build can decode. An upstream change that renumbers or removes the ROCMFP* ids breaks interoperation with charlie12345/ROCmFPX artifacts even on a build that cannot decode them.
wins.notes: protected_paths names only the two subtrees that are wholly this mechanism. The shared core files it also touches (ggml.h, ggml.c, ggml-quants.c, ggml-cpu.c, ops.cpp, llama.h, llama-model-loader.cpp, llama-quant.cpp, quantize.cpp, gguf-py/gguf/constants.py) are guarded by the ANCHOR half instead, deliberately: those files change on nearly every bump, and pinning them as paths would refuse every sync for a reason that is almost never the real one. The anchors catch what actually threatens this win - a renumbering or removal of the type/ftype ids. That is a signal-to-noise choice and it is named here so it can be revisited, not discovered.

This DIVERGES DELIBERATELY from PrismML's upstream default of ON. It is a different object from the kernel it gates - `cpu-vnni-repack-dual-residency` protects the kernel, and every anchor of that entry would still resolve after this default was flipped back.

wins.quality_gate: ENGAGEMENT re-verified in BOTH arms on one binary with only the env flip: unset produces no `load_tensors: CPU_REPACK model buffer size` line at all, `=1` produces it (4.68 MiB on the g64 fixture), and both arms return coherent text with no NaN. A default that reads as OFF but still allocates the repack buffer has not passed this gate.

wins.mechanism: Heat-aware MoE cache eviction: each slot counts resident uses, and the victim picker prefers the least-recently-used slot at or below the hot threshold, falling back to the LRU head only when every eligible slot is hot. wins.mechanism: Two things, neither of which changes a default. (1) A receipt: one GGML_LOG_INFO per distinct MUL_MAT_ID B-staging mode per process - contiguous | K-padded | q8_1 - naming coopmat2, both source types, ne10, the staged row stride and ne11, so an A/B log proves which path the dispatch took. Upstream 77f132cb1's K-padded staging is a coopmat2 requirement (its B decode callback does not bounds-check K); on a coopmat1/scalar device the padded mode is never selected and this line is the runtime witness of that. No override is offered on purpose. (2) A hazard assert: the fork's tq_rotate staging wins the tq_rotate / y_needs_reformat ladder and copies B CONTIGUOUS f32 while stride_b_y still follows y_needs_k_padding, so GGML_ASSERT(!(tq_rotate && y_needs_k_padding)) aborts instead of reading B with a padded stride over an unpadded copy.
wins.quality_gate: No default and no dispatch changes, so the arms are the same kernel: 48 MUL_MAT_ID ops, 3 rounds per arm, correctness unchanged. The assert converts a silent wrong-math read into an abort.
wins.workload: Radeon 780M (gfx1103, Vulkan0, coopmat1 - no coopmat2), test-backend-ops MUL_MAT_ID op ladder plus seven server logs read for the receipt.
wins.measured_effect: DOCUMENTED-TAKE, and the receipt is the result: 0 K-padded rows in 7 logs, so the upstream K-padding path CANNOT engage on this GPU. Op ladder x0.976 to x1.032, no CI claimed at n=3. The real cure for the hazard - padded f32 rotate staging - is OWED to the off-rig lane where a coopmat2 device exists.
wins.notes: The protectable thing is the receipt line and the assert. Removing either restores a state where a wrong staging mode is unprovable from a log, and where the rotate x padding combination computes garbage instead of aborting.

wins.mechanism: The UMA read-back direct memcpy is taken only when the buffer's OWN matched memory type is HOST_CACHED, probed per call from the flags stored at allocation, instead of unconditionally for every host-visible buffer on a UMA device. An uncached mapping falls through to the staging branch that every non-UMA host-visible (rebar) buffer already uses. GGML_ARIFI_UMA_READ_PATH = auto (default, probe) | direct (upstream behaviour) | staging (always staging). One stderr receipt per process names the resolved path and the env value, because llama-server drops ggml INFO records. Writes are untouched: write-combined is the right mode for CPU writes.
wins.quality_gate: Bit-identical by construction: the same bytes, copied by the copy engine instead of the CPU. F-141 recorded in the cell; no arithmetic is touched.
wins.workload: Radeon 780M (gfx1103, Vulkan0), UMA device whose host-visible mapping is NOT host-cached, seat line plus four c3 files; lane209 palindrome.
wins.measured_effect: DOCUMENTED-TAKE, flat. Mechanism cell (ONE binary, direct vs auto) read decode +0.21% CI95 [-0.26%, +0.69%] - one of the two quietest cells in the whole wave. The four c3 files land within -1.88% and -0.03% on DFlash2 decode. Cell c1 was NOT BANKED (resumed across the 21:30 job). OWED: a host-cached unified-memory device, which is where the probe would actually select direct and where the fix can pay.
wins.notes: Origin is ucicelos/flashnext-hybrid fix 3 ('boundary tensors read through the wrong memory mapping'); the Vulkan/UMA port is native to ArifiLabs.

wins.mechanism: GGML_TYPE_SX8 = 57: the MarlaLabs S-X8 v4.3 weight format (dmin/dmax f16 + 4 x 2-bit range strategy + 6-bit levels, 30 B / 32, 7.50 bpw) as a CPU decoder - dequant, vec_dot against q8_1, and the GET_ROWS / CPY / SET_ROWS arms - plus gguf-py constants and test-backend-ops coverage. Retagged from the author's id 41, which this tree spends on upstream Q1_0, under the fork's type-id arbitration; tools/gguf-retag-sx8/retag_sx8.py rewrites a file's ids on a COPY and refuses unless every id-41 tensor spans exactly 30 B / 32 values. OPT-IN BY TYPE NAME: no env, no build flag, no default moved, so any launch that does not name the type is byte-identical to the pre-port engine.
wins.quality_gate: Codec cross-check against the author's reference (tools/gguf-retag-sx8/test_sx8_codec.py) plus the test-backend-ops rows for the type; no S-X8 file exists on the estate, so an end-to-end quality cell is OWED, not claimed.
wins.workload: CPU path only. The harmless cell measured the port PRESENT and UNREACHABLE on the seat line (Radeon 780M, Vulkan0, Huihui UD-Q4_K_XL), which is what proves it costs nothing when unused.

wins.mechanism: GGML_TYPE_TBQ3_0 = 58 (d + qs[48], signed FWHT + 8 Lloyd-Max centroids, 50 B / 128) and GGML_TYPE_TBQ4_0 = 59 (d + qs[64], 16 centroids, 66 B / 128), ported from jtrefon/llama.cpp-turboq-mtp and retagged from the author's 42/43 under the fork's type-id arbitration. CPU reference only: every backend without a kernel must report them not supported, never a wrong value. OPT-IN BY TYPE NAME (-ctk/-ctv tbq4_0), so no default moves. Two guards ride with them: LLAMA_ALLOW_TBQ3_KV (default OFF) refuses a tbq3_0 V cache, which the source fork measured collapsing into token repetition, and warns on tbq3_0 K; and a runtime DEVICE guard refuses a TBQ KV cache at context init when the offload device cannot run SET_ROWS into it, instead of letting the scheduler abort at graph time.
wins.opt_out: -nkvo, -dev none, or a supported KV type (the device guard); LLAMA_ALLOW_TBQ3_KV=1 (the 3-bit KV quality guard)
wins.quality_gate: test-quantize-fns rows for both types; the tbq3_0 V-cache refusal is itself the quality guard, carried from the source fork's 2026-08-11 measurement (Qwen3.5-4B, CPU path). An end-to-end quality cell on a TBQ KV cache is OWED.
wins.workload: Radeon 780M (gfx1103, Vulkan0) for the harmless cell; the KV cells ran at KV-on-host on a 0.515 t/s crawl and did not complete.
wins.measured_effect: DOCUMENTED-TAKE. Harmless cell (types present, no launch names them): DFlash2 decode +0.60% CI95 [-1.28%, +2.47%], DFlash2 prefill +8.15% [+5.38%, +10.92%] - the latter pure build floor. THE KV MECHANISM WAS NEVER MEASURED: the baseline arm refused the type ('Unsupported cache type: tbq4_0') and the candidate arm was aborted by the schedule horizon. What ran is engine-vs-engine at KV-on-host, +1.60% [+1.30%, +1.90%] on a 0.515 t/s crawl, which is not a claim about TBQ.
wins.notes: The re-run design is named: candidate-engine tbq4_0 vs candidate-engine q8_0. A baseline-engine arm is impossible, because the base engine does not know the type - that is what produced the refusal.
